results.content:
Title: Knock: Knock on your MacBook to control your Mac | Product Hunt
# Knock. ## Knock on your MacBook to control your Mac. ### Trending products. @will\_gee1 This is one of those ideas that sounds like a gimmick until you actually think about the use cases. The fact that you built a live sensitivity tuner shows you've thought about the real problem here, which isn't detecting a knock - it's not detecting everything else. Like if I'm at a coffee shop and someone bumps the table, or if I'm typing aggressively - does the accelerometer distinguish between a deliberate knock pattern and ambient vibration? Also curious whether you've considered double-knock or triple-knock as separate triggers. Really creative use of hardware that's just sitting there unused. You’re exactly right that the hard part isn’t detecting a knock, it’s filtering everything else. Knock looks for short vibration spikes that match the timing of a tap rather than general motion, which helps separate a deliberate knock from background desk movement. It also temporarily pauses detection while you’re typing. Sensitivity can also be tuned depending on the desk setup, and the Knock Test view lets you see the accelerometer waveform in real time so users can dial it in. And yes, single, double and triple knocks are all separate triggers right now, so you can map different actions to each. The main difference is that Knock focuses on physical interaction with your Mac. Instead of using the keyboard or opening a launcher like Raycast, you can trigger actions just by tapping your MacBook. It’s meant to be a quick, hands-free layer on top of macOS for things like muting audio, pausing music, or triggering actions while you’re away from the keyboard. That’s exactly how I think about it - not a replacement for Raycast/Alfred, just something that fits in when you’re not on the keyboard. Knock reads that motion data and looks for very short impulse spikes that match the pattern of a tap on the laptop chassis or the desk it's sitting on. There’s a sensitivity slider so people can tune it for their setup, and gestures are also temporarily suppressed while typing to prevent false triggers.

results.content:
Title: Control My Mac: A shortcut deck for every Mac app, on your iPhone or iPad | Product Hunt
# Control My Mac. ## A shortcut deck for every Mac app, on your iPhone or iPad. ## A shortcut deck for every Mac app, on your iPhone or iPad. Control My Mac turns your iPhone or iPad into a trackpad, keyboard and shortcut deck for your Mac, built so the whole Mac works with one finger. Its Grid of shortcut buttons switches automatically to match the Mac app in front. Write long messages on your phone and send them in one go. Launch apps and switch windows. Pair with one QR scan: no account, no servers, no ads, and an encrypted direct connection. The Mac app is free. Launch tags:Mac•Productivity•Inclusivity. WinRAR download free and support. Dropbox SignSimple, secure eSignatures for the way your team works. No reviews yetBe the first to leave a review for Control My Mac. Hey Product Hunt, Sebastian here. I built Control My Mac because I kept getting up from the couch to click one thing on my Mac mini under the TV. Then I realised a lot of people have a much better reason than me to not reach the keyboard: an injury, RSI, a cast, a baby asleep on one arm. So the whole thing is built around one finger. Your iPhone or iPad becomes: • a trackpad (move, click, right click, scroll) • a keyboard, live key by key, or write the whole message first and send it in one go • a Grid of shortcut buttons that switches automatically depending on which Mac app is in front • an app launcher and window switcher A few things I cared about: • No account, no servers, no ads. The phone talks straight to the Mac over Wi-Fi or Bluetooth, encrypted. • Pairing is one QR scan. No IP addresses, no firewall stuff. The iPhone app has a free Essentials tier. Full App is an optional upgrade with a 7-day free trial, and there's a one-time Lifetime option if you hate subscriptions (me too). I'd really like to hear how you'd use it and what's missing. I'm reading every comment today.
